criteria.evidence: Parser/well-formedness (checker analogue: §16.1/§16.2 object admission + §12 closed schemas). checker/src/object/lexical.rs validates canonical INT/FLOAT spellings, type widths, bounds, spacing and the empty-regs exception before hashing, and the 1,933-case numeric/punctuation differential (checker/tests/lexical_differential.rs) passes with 0 disagreements; my i04 and bounds-spacing probes are now rejected by both checker and pinned interpreter, and cert claim/kind/domain/sampler schemas are closed (eval/replay_claim.rs validate_shape, cert.rs check_claim). But admission is not grammar-complete: lexical.rs never checks that an instruction word is a §4 OPCODE mnemonic (opcode_widths only checks NAME shape and dotted INT widths) and gap() admits an empty bounds clause, so Object::parse admits texts the pinned interpreter's hash and check reject (blocking M1, rung 4(a)). Borrow-frame first/last/lifetime/domain/sampler shapes are also only presence-checked before an unchecked deferral (eval/borrow_frames.rs).
criteria.change: Enforce the remaining §16.2 word/grammar contexts at admission for every function (OPCODE mnemonic set, non-empty bounds INT list), in lexical.rs/Object::parse, before any hash is computed.

criteria.evidence: Identity/linking (checker analogue: §9.2 recomputation). Hash bindings are recomputed from supplied bytes and producer hashes never trusted (cert.rs establishes line; params_hash now fails closed on JCS error instead of unwrap_or_default, signature/bounds JCS comparisons fail to reject not to accept); plausible wrong-hash mutations reject with E_CERT_BINDING (mutation_sweep.rs) and published hash witnesses pass (hashes.rs in the 291-test green run). One localised hole: hashes are computed for texts that are not §16 objects at all (M1: checker reports a recomputed object_hash for an object whose identity the pinned interpreter's hash command refuses), so identity is only as sound as admission.
criteria.change: Gate hashing on full §16.2 admission (the M1 fix); no other identity change needed.
